subject: Clarification request: APAC hosting options and fallback behavior for RFP - Sumitomo
messages:
From: Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@sumitomo-biz.co.jp>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 +0900
Subject: Clarification: APAC hosting & data locality options for RFP

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the RFP materials. A few follow-ups from our compliance and procurement teams (Sec 3.2 - Data Residency). Could you please clarify the following items specifically for APAC?

1) Physical processing location: For hosted Redwood API calls from our Tokyo region customers, can you guarantee request/response processing (including KV/prefix cache access) occurs only in Tokyo (JP) physical infrastructure, not routed to Singapore or other regions?

2) Cache and ephemeral storage: If we enable prefix/KV caching, is any cached content replicated or moved across regions? Can we configure caches to be Tokyo-only?

3) Fallback behavior: If Tokyo capacity is exhausted, what is the default fallback region? Can we opt out of automatic fallback for specific workloads (PII-sensitive)?

4) KMS and key control: Do you support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) scoped to the Tokyo region? Is the envelope key material ever exported or stored outside Tokyo?

5) Audit logs and residency of logs: Are request logs, traces, and usage records stored in Tokyo? What retention controls are available?

6) Contractual language: Please provide suggested SOW/contract wording we can include to require Tokyo-only processing for defined endpoints, and any limitations or SLAs around that guarantee.

We have a short deadline for this RFP loop; would appreciate a consolidated response with any attachments or diagrams.

Regards,
Kenji Sato
Senior IT Procurement Manager
Sumitomo Financial Services

--
Reference: Sumitomo RFP Section 3.2 (Data Residency).

Subject: Re: Clarification: APAC hosting & data locality options for RFP

Hi Kenji — thanks for the clear questions. Below is a consolidated response; I’ve attached an APAC deployment matrix and a simple flow diagram that shows how fallback decisions are made. I’ll call out where additional contractual commitments are possible and where technical constraints apply.

1) Physical processing location
- Hosted API (standard): By default, requests from clients in Japan are routed to Tokyo-hosted capacity when available. We can provide a Tokyo-only routing policy for specific endpoints to ensure all CPU/GPU inference, KV lookups, and prefix cache reads happen on Tokyo hosts.
- Note: For the hosted multitenant pool, there is a small provisioning window where traffic may be routed to a compatible region during capacity shortages unless explicitly restricted.

2) Cache and ephemeral storage
- Prefix/KV cache can be configured as Tokyo-scoped. When Tokyo-scoped caching is enabled, cached objects are stored only on Tokyo nodes and are not replicated to other regions.
- Ephemeral runtime artifacts (e.g., GPU memory, local disk swap) are always transient and are cleared per-session; we provide a TTL policy you can set.

3) Fallback behavior
- Default behavior: auto-fallback to Singapore (ap-southeast-1) when Tokyo is saturated. This helps maintain latency and availability.
- Opt-out: For contracts and SOWs we sign, we can set a policy to disable cross-region fallback for named endpoints and workloads; in that case, requests that cannot be served in Tokyo will return a 503 with a retry recommendation.

4) KMS and key control
- We support customer-managed KMS via CloudKMS/HSM integrations. Keys can be provisioned and scoped to the Tokyo region. Envelope keys used by Redwood will not be exported outside the region when Tokyo-scoped KMS is selected.

5) Audit logs and retention
- Request logs, tracing metadata, and billing records for Tokyo-scoped endpoints can be retained in Tokyo storage. We offer configurable retention (30/90/365 days) and can provide a dedicated logs bucket in your cloud tenant via a Private deployment arrangement.

6) Contractual language
- Suggested clause (draft): "Redwood Inference will route and process requests for the Contracted Tokyo Endpoints solely within Tokyo region physical infrastructure. In the event of Tokyo capacity exhaustion, Redwood will not route Contracted Tokyo Endpoints to other regions unless Customer provides written authorization; instead Redwood will return an availability error and retry guidance."
- We note this clause is available for Dedicated and Private deployments as a standard commitment; for Hosted multitenant customers we can include it in a negotiated SOW with capacity commitments (see attachments).

Next steps
- Attached: APAC_Deployment_Matrix.xlsx, Tokyo-SG-Fallback-Flow.png, SOC2_AIP.pdf (redacted).
- Can we schedule a 30-minute call to finalize the SOW wording? I’m available Mon Apr 5 09:00-11:30 JST or Tue Apr 6 14:00-17:00 JST — please let me know what suits your team.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
[email signature]

Subject: Re: Clarification: APAC hosting & data locality options for RFP

Tessa — adding a couple of technical clarifications you can paste into the response:

- KV/prefix cache behavior: Tokyo-scoped caches are implemented at the node-local level with a Tokyo-only replication policy. That means there is no background replication to other regions when Tokyo-scoped is selected.
- Cold start model loading: If a particular model shard is not present on Tokyo nodes (rare for our curated set), model weights may be pulled from regional object storage; for Tokyo-only guarantees we pin the model shards to Tokyo hosts under Dedicated/Private.
- Routing: Our smart routing uses capacity, latency, and SLO policy. For Hosted customers who take the Tokyo-only routing option, we enforce a policy that overrides smart-routing to disallow cross-region fallback; this will surface in the client as an error code 421 with an explanatory message.

Happy to join the SOW call and answer any low-level questions — I can cover cache TTL knobs and model placement guarantees.

Connor O’Brien
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime
